title: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 fixes 23 vulnerabilities across VMware products, including ESX and vCenter
date_note: Broadcom's advisory is dated by its initial publication day; no earlier day is given.
geo_basis: vendor (Broadcom, advisory publisher); the flaws affect users worldwide
summary: Broadcom published advisory VMSA-2026-0011 on 24 November, fixing 23 vulnerabilities in VMware products. Rapid7 says CVE-2026-123903, an authentication bypass in vCenter's VMware Directory Service, has a Broadcom CVSSv3.1 score of 9.8 and a public proof-of-concept exploit that Rapid7 validated; it knows of no public reports of exploitation. Rapid7 recommends urgent remediation outside normal patching cycles.
plain: Broadcom fixed 23 VMware flaws, including a critical vCenter login bypass. Rapid7 says a public proof-of-concept exploit works and recommends urgent patching.
exec: Rapid7 says a public exploit works against a critical vCenter flaw (CVSSv3.1 9.8) fixed in Broadcom's advisory.
action: Rapid7 recommends remediating exposed systems on an urgent basis outside of normal patching cycles; Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0011 lists the fixed version for each product, and for ESX and vCenter 7.0 contact Broadcom support.

evidence.quote: Broadcom released VMSA-2026-0011 on November 24, 2026, fixing 23 vulnerabilities.
CVE-2026-123910 is a heap out-of-bounds write, and CVE-2026-123911 is a use-after-free.
Broadcom assigned it a CVSSv3.1 score of 9.8 Critical.
As of this writing, there are no known public reports of exploitation of CVE-2026-123903 in the wild.

validation.note: Broadcom's own advisory VMSA-2026-0011 and Securityonline agree on the date and the 23 CVEs.

review.note: title, date, 23 CVE IDs, 9.8, PoC, no exploitation, 7.0 support note against Broadcom, Rapid7, Securityonline
